blurb: American water retriever with an oily, wavy, waterproof coat in brown, sedge or deadgrass
description: The Chesapeake Bay Retriever is a large American retriever from Maryland with a wavy, oily, waterproof coat, bred for icy-water duck work; bright and loyal.
answer: The Chesapeake Bay Retriever is a large American retriever developed around Maryland's Chesapeake Bay in the 19th century. It was used to retrieve waterfowl, pull fishing nets and rescue fishermen, and is now mainly a family pet and hunting companion. It stands about 53 to 66 cm and weighs 25 to 37 kg.

body: The breed traces back to two pups, Sailor and Canton, rescued from a foundering ship off Maryland in 1807 and described as Newfoundland or St. John's water dogs. They were bred with local dogs, including spaniels and hounds, with ability valued over pedigree. The American Kennel Club recognized a single Chesapeake Bay Retriever type in 1918, with few changes to the standard since. In 1964 it became the official dog of Maryland.

It resembles a Labrador but has a wavy coat, clear yellowish or amber eyes, hindquarters as high as or slightly higher than the shoulders, webbed toes and a powerful chest. The thick double coat is harsh outside and woolly underneath, feels slightly oily and resists water; it may have a slight musky odour. Accepted colours are brown, sedge and deadgrass, with white allowed only in small spots on the breast, belly or feet.

The breed standard describes a bright and happy disposition, intelligence, quiet good sense and an affectionate, protective nature. Some Chesapeakes are assertive, willful and reserved with strangers, while others are outgoing. Some grin by baring their front teeth, a sign of joy rather than a threat. With proper socialization they are described as excellent family dogs.

Coat care is minimal, mainly weekly brushing; over-bathing can strip the protective oil. Trainers now recommend consistent daily obedience work with play. The breed competes in field trials, hunt tests, obedience, agility and tracking and is known for stamina.

A UK Kennel Club survey put median lifespan at 10.75 years. Conditions reported in the breed include exercise-induced collapse, hip dysplasia, progressive retinal atrophy, type 3 von Willebrand disease, cataract, regional alopecia and degenerative myelopathy.

faq.q: How big does a Chesapeake Bay Retriever get?
faq.a: It stands about 53 to 66 cm at the withers and weighs about 25 to 37 kg.

faq.q: Are Chesapeake Bay Retrievers good family dogs?
faq.a: They are described as excellent family dogs when properly socialized, though some can be willful and reserved with strangers.

faq.q: Is the Chesapeake Bay Retriever recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 263 in Group 8.
